questions.question: You index PDFs from Azure Blob Storage with an Azure AI Search indexer and a skillset that includes the OCR skill. Scanned PDFs still return no text. What should you configure?

options.text: Set imageAction to generateNormalizedImages on the indexer
options.why: Correct. The OCR skill only receives images when document cracking extracts them, and this setting provides them.

options.text: Increase the number of replicas on the search service
options.why: Replicas add query capacity. They do not change what the indexer extracts.

options.text: Add a semantic configuration to the index
options.why: A semantic configuration affects query-time ranking, not text extraction.

options.text: Change the data source to use an account key
options.why: The authentication method does not affect whether images are passed to OCR.

questions.explanation: The indexer must be configured to extract images (imageAction set to generateNormalizedImages) so that the OCR skill has input.

questions.question: A RAG index must return individual passages from 200-page PDFs, each linked to its source file. Which combination should you use in the skillset?

options.text: The Text Split skill and index projections
options.why: Correct. Text Split creates chunks and index projections write each chunk as its own search document with a parent key.

options.text: The PII Detection skill and a synonym map
options.why: These protect data and expand terms. They do not create chunks.

options.text: The Key Phrase Extraction skill and a scoring profile
options.why: Key phrases summarise content. They do not divide a file into passages.

options.text: A single index document per file and a larger vector dimension
options.why: A file-sized document returns whole files, and dimensions do not control chunking.

questions.explanation: Chunking plus index projections gives one search document per chunk with a link to its parent.

questions.question: An indexer must read a blob container without storing a connection string or key. Which two actions are required?

options.text: Enable a managed identity on the storage account and assign it Search Service Contributor
options.why: The search service is the caller, so the role must be granted to its identity on the storage account.

options.text: Assign the Owner role to the indexer on the subscription
options.why: Indexers are not role assignees, and Owner is far more than needed.

options.text: Create a shared access signature and store it in the index
options.why: A SAS is still a secret to manage, and it must not be stored in the index.

options.text: Enable a system-assigned managed identity on the search service and assign it Storage Blob Data Reader on the storage account
options.why: Correct. The data source then authenticates as the service identity with a read-only data role.

questions.explanation: Use the search service's managed identity with Storage Blob Data Reader to avoid keys.

questions.question: You change the chunk size in the Text Split skill. After the next scheduled run the index still contains the old chunks. What should you do?

options.text: Delete the data source and recreate it with the same name
options.why: This is unnecessary. A reset of the indexer is sufficient.

options.text: Reset the indexer and run it again
options.why: Correct. Blob change detection skips unchanged files, so a reset is needed to process every document again.

options.text: Scale the search service to a higher tier
options.why: Capacity does not make the indexer revisit unchanged files.

options.text: Disable the semantic ranker
options.why: The ranker has no effect on how documents are indexed.

questions.explanation: Unchanged blobs are skipped, so pipeline changes require an indexer reset.

questions.question: You must make recorded support calls searchable in Azure AI Search. Which two approaches meet the requirement?

options.text: Analyze the recordings with Azure Content Understanding and index the returned transcript text
options.why: Correct. Analysis produces transcripts and segments that can then be indexed.

options.text: Add the OCR skill to read the audio files
options.why: OCR reads text in images. It does not process audio.

options.text: Set the semantic ranker to read the audio
options.why: The ranker reorders text results. It does not ingest audio.

options.text: Transcribe the audio with Azure Speech and upload the text to the index
options.why: Correct. The transcript becomes searchable text.

questions.explanation: Indexers do not transcribe audio themselves. Convert the audio to text first, then index it.
